utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances, please, for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis and Matthias Neuner for the Prosecution, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And could we have for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, and good morning to the colleagues from the Prosecution and everyone in and around the courtroom. I am Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for the Defence of General Rasim Delic, with our case manager, Lejla Gluhic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Mr. Husic, good morning to you. I know you know this by now, but it's still my duty to remind you that you made a declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth, and that you are still bound by that declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note, the witness's microphones are off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Husic.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yesterday, we stopped at the point where we were talking about combat of the Mujahedin or the El Mudjahedin Detachment outside the area of responsibility of the 306th Brigade, and I want to continue this morning on that course. Could we please have document PT2141 shown to this witness. While it is being displayed, this is a document from the 5th of June, 1995, and it is entitled: "Weekly Information on the Military and Political Situation in the RBiH for Subordinated Units." You can see the title here on the first page, Mr. Husic. If we could for a moment go to the last page. I'm interested in the signature. Whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: This is my signature on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you authored that report; right?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I haven't authored it, but I -- I signed them, and the reports are prepared by the clerks. This is not a report, though. This is just information for the fighters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could go back to page 1, please. And on page 1 -- it's, in English, actually page 2, page 1 of the B/C/S. Please look at the section 2. It is within this section 2 the second paragraph, and in English it is, page 2, the second paragraph. We see here mentioning of Zavidovici and Ozren, and "of our forces (the 35th Division) who were involved in active defence and primary tasks involved in offensive combat activities in the 328 Mountain Brigade zone of responsibility, where excellent results were accomplished." The next paragraph, as you can see then, talks about: "The El Mudjahedin Detachment contributed considerably in the course of the above-mentioned combat activities, inflicting massive losses to the aggressor." Could you explain to me how you obtained that information at the time?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I explained yesterday that these bits of information that we sent to the fighters on the lines of defence were taken off from the media, and the clerks who were in charge of this would write down whatever was reported in the media, collected it and compiled, and then sent it as information to the fighters of our units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I ask that the document be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1208.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, the information that was picked up from the media, was that information that was available throughout the country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move on to the next document, PT2121, please. It's, while it comes up, a report from the 29th of May, 1995, same category, a report on the military and political situation in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina for subordinated units, and if we could for a second focus on the last page and the signature there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, am I correct in saying that this is your signature?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could go back, in English, to page 3, and in B/C/S to page 1. And again it is section 2 I am interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look at the eighth line in the B/C/S version of section 2, for the English it is page 3, the first paragraph. And we see here that the following information is provided: "On the 27th of May, the units of the 35th Division (the El Mujahedin Detachment was in charge of the task) took control of the facilities of Podsjelovo, [indiscernible], Gaj, Prijedor, inflicting heavy losses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second. We are waiting for the page to be turned in the English. We are behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It's actually the first paragraph on this page 3 which is displayed here in front of you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where are you reading from?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm reading -- I started at line 1.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here that it was reported that the 35th Division forces, including the Mujahedin, inflicted heavy losses to the aggressor troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where did you get this information from?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Also from the media, from the area that is some few hundred kilometres from the area of responsibility of the 36th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "306th Brigade," interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could my distinguished Colleague Neuner always point out the date for the witness's benefit on the document so that the witness understands what is being discussed, because it is my impression that the witness believes that there is -- that this is a discussion about 1992. So just to make sure there is no misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When the document was brought up, we were told that it's a document dated the 29th of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I believe I have done so, too, but I cannot scroll the transcript back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You did tell us. That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you just tell me this last line of the section I was just reading? It says here: "Our soldiers showed the Chetniks how to fight on a battlefield." What did you mean by that portion in the document which you signed?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I am not the author of this document, as I pointed out earlier. The clerk, who is in charge of information-taking, the information from the media, he compiled this, and as assistant commander in the brigade, I signed these documents and forwarded them to the subordinate fighters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, you know what? In law, when you put your signature on a document, you're adopting that document as your own. We don't know who that clerk is. We see the person who signed the document, and we want the person who signed the document. Can you please stop telling us about a clerk. This is your document. Okay? And answer questions, because you've adopted the document as your own. Didn't you read it before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I cannot answer as to the meaning of this sentence. It means what it says there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Look. If you didn't understand the meaning of the sentence at the time you signed the document, you should have told the clerk to change it. And if you didn't, it means you understood. You must then answer questions on it. We are not playing marbles here, okay. We are serious. Don't hide behind tracks who are not here. You're wasting our time. Now, answer your questions honestly and truthfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in your position as assistant commander of morale of the 3rd Corps, at the time you had the authority to take that sentence out if you disagreed, Mr. Husic?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask that the document be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document will become Exhibit number 1209.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You have talked yesterday about Operation Farz in September 1995, and is it correct that President Izetbegovic visited at the second or third day after the beginning of Operation Farz, when Vozuca had been liberated?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And, in fact, you, as assistant commander for morale of the 3rd Corps, prepared, with others, the reception of Mr. Izetbegovic in the area of Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were in charge of protocol.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to show you two small excerpts on a video now and would ask you to recognise persons. I will first play the tape to you and would then ask you to tell us whom you recognised. Could we have, please, from Exhibit 409, a small excerpt shown now. And I'm referring here to a portion about a minute starting at time code 40 minutes and 55 seconds. I'm informed it starts at 40 minutes 25 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anybody here?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. On President Izetbegovic's right-hand side, on the left-hand side of the screen, is Sakib Mahmuljin. On the other side of President Izetbegovic is the commander of the 35th Division, Fadil Hasanagic. Behind the president, I think of the two persons shown, I'm not sure whether one of them is Mr. Ribo Haso, it could be, but I'm not absolutely certain, and the other person is Abu Maali, the commander of the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I, with the assistance of the usher, have -- still handed out to the witness, and this is PT6166.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which is PT616?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: 6166 is the PT number assigned to this still by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, please. Could you -- we are having some technical problems. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please mark, above the head of Mr. Izetbegovic, a number 1.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Above the head of Mr. Hasanagic a number 2, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Above the head of Mr. Mahmuljin a number 3.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Above the head of whom you believe to be Haso Ribo a number 4.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And above the head of Mr. Abu Maali, a number 5, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please sign with today's date, adding today's date, the 13th of March.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution offers this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor -- or, rather, Mr. Witness, do you know the gentleman to the left rear of the late president, the gentleman sporting a beard and wearing a white cap?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: PT6166 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was 6166.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 6166, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1211.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours. This will be 1210.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I now wish to play a second excerpt from Exhibit 409 to you, and the time code is 43 minutes 35 seconds until 44 minutes 56 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whom you recognised on this excerpt?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: The first person whose head you can see only is the assistant commander for security of the 3rd Corps, Mr. Ekrem Alihodzic. The second person with grey hair, I don't know. The third person is the commander of the 2nd Corps of the RBiH Army, Mr. Sead Delic, and the fourth person is Mr. Bakir Alispahic, but I'm not sure what position he was on at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has another still. It is PT6168.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark, above the head of Mr. Ekrem Alihodzic, a number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And next to the nose of Saed Delic, a number 2, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How about on his cheek?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Or on his cheek, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And again on the cheek of Mr. Bakir Alispahic, a number 3, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I'm putting to you that Mr. Bakir Alispahic was at the time the Minister of Interior, what would you say?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: It is possible, but I really don't know. I'm not sure:

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution offers this document or this still into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: PT6168 is admitted -- I beg your pardon. PT6168 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit number 1211.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And from this sequence, the Prosecution has produced a second still. This is PT6170.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Whom do you recognise here?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: In the front is the late President Izetbegovic. Behind him, the first person on his right-hand side, but on the screen on the left-hand side, is the commander of the 3rd Corps, Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin. The person next to him, on his right side, is Abu Maali, and the person next to him, the person with a beard, is Ajman. I don't know his name. I just know that he was called "Ajman."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark, above the head of Mr. Izetbegovic, a "1." I'm told on the forehead.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You have just marked -- then please continue -- you've just marked it above his head. Could you continue to mark a "2" on the forehead of Mr. Mahmuljin.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: A "3" on the forehead of Abu Maali.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And a "4" on the forehead of the person Ajman or referred to as "Ajman."

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution offers this document -- this still into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: PT6170 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit 1212.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move back to 1993 now and the events in late May, early June 1993 in the Bila Valley. I want to show you, first of all, a map. This is D1044. While the map is being displayed: Do you agree with me that before the war, Croats and Muslims or Bosniaks lived in the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And especially in the upper part of the Bila Valley, there were almost exclusively Bosniak persons living?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, in a part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I don't see the map being displayed. I was asking for D1044. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you, first of all, agree that this is a portion -- or this map depicts a portion of the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And we talked yesterday about Gluha Bukovica. Gluha Bukovica is in the upper part of the Bila Valley which is not depicted on this portion of the map; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Maybe we can scroll it a little bit up. Yes. The other way, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In Gluha Bukovica, there were mainly Bosniaks living at the beginning of the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Also in Dub?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Not in Mehurici. In Mehurici, there were Croats and Serbs and Bosniaks, but the Bosniaks were in a majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in Jezerci?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: In Jezerci, the inhabitants were Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in Podovi, the inhabitants were Bosniaks, too?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: These are not Podlugovi but Podovi, and the population was mixed. In half of the settlement, there were Croats, and the other half was inhabited by Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in Krpeljici, this was --

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: As for Krpeljici, the majority were Bosniaks, but in the left part of the village there were mixed houses of Croats and Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would it be asking too much if we asked that you mark these places that you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to do this in the next step. Okay, we will do it right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please mark Dub with a number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mehurici with a number 2.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Jezerci with a number 3.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Podovi with a number 4.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Krpeljici with the number 5.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I'm going on with the villages now. Guca Gora, could you tell us -- could you first of all mark a number 6?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell us what the dominant population in Guca Gora was?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: The majority population of Guca Gora were Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Radonjici with the number 7.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the majority population was Croat?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Bukovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: There are two Bukovicas, the large and the small one, so one is Croat and the other Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So could you mark the Croat one with an "8."

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the Bosniak part of Bukovica with a "9."

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Miletici was a Croat-inhabited location?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Possibly, but there were Bosniaks living there as well as Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark the Bosniak part with a "10"?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks] It is one settlement. They're not separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then I misunderstood you. Then mark the entire part of Miletici with the number 10, please. And if we could go to Maline, you agree with me that there were two parts in Maline, it had a mixed population?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In Gornji Maline, Croats were living, and if you could mark that with a number 11 if you agree.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You agree, yes, that there were Croats living?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in Donje Maline, Bosniaks were living?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark that with a "12," please. And if I understood your testimony correct yesterday, you, by the 28th of May, 1993, got stuck with Mr. Sipic and other officers in Krpeljici, which you have marked with the number 5. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You have been also shown yesterday Exhibit 90, referring to the death of Sakib Brkic, a person from Dub village. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if I remember correctly, the document said that, and Your Honours asked you about this, he was killed in the Probijeno Brdo sector. This is elevation 1009, by the Frankopan Brigade. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In the what sector?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Probjeno Brdo sector, and I will ask the witness about this, at elevation 1009.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you remember? Do you remember talking about this document and Mr. Sakib Brkic yesterday?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you point out on this map where Probijeno Brdo, elevation 1009, is, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: The name of the elevation is something I have never heard, but I know it's close to the village of Suhi Dol.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you maybe mark Suhi Dol with a "13."

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. So it was near the village of Suhi Dol where Mr. Brkic was killed; right?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We were talking about the combat activities which were going on. Could you enlighten the Chamber? At the beginning of June, when you were getting stuck, where about was the confrontation line between the ARBiH and the HVO, before the outbreak of the combat activities?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: As you can see, the settlements have mixed populations, and there was a -- there wasn't a definite line. All the Bosniak villages in this area southeast of Mehurici were blocked, each one of them individually. And on the 4th of May, after the ultimatum given to the villages of Velika Bukovica, Radonjici --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting you. I was only interested with the situation of the forces not on the 4th of May but at the beginning of June; late May 1993, beginning of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I thought you were referring to the 4th of May. So what I just said applied to the 4th of May, 1993. The villages of Velika Bukovica, Bandol --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Tell us about June.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I was asking the position of the forces, HVO forces and ARBiH forces, at the beginning of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: June, thanks.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: The positions were such that there were trenches around each village. There wasn't a line, and the HVO held the dominating elevations above the villages of Maline Kljake and the village of Velika Bukovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell us which villages, and you can just refer to numbers here, were controlled by the HVO at the beginning of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: You mean which belonged to them or which they had encircled and surrounded?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which belonged to them? And we will come to encircled later.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: The villages of Mala Bukovica --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just refer to numbers. The HVO held the following villages. Could you please tell the numbers just?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Number 8, Radonjici; number 7, Gornji Maline; number 11, Guca Gora; number 12, a part of Podovi; number 4 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which is number 6? You say number 12 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... number 12, unless I'm hearing something that I shouldn't hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So can I summarise?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: 8, 7, 11 and 6, and Podovi, 4, were held by the HVO at the beginning of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: And a number of villages in the southeastern part of this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You're referring to the area of Han Bila?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark that Han Bila maybe or the southern part -- you said "east part," southeast part -- the area southeast of Han Bila where --

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think we have used number 13 at Suhi Dol.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 14. I was mistaken. I apologise. 14.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And is it correct to say that the following villages were held by the ARBiH, and I'm just proposing numbers to you, if you could just say "yes," number 13 --

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Dub, number 1?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Miletici, number 10?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Miletici were mixed. There were Croats and Bosniaks living there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you say the villages you were mentioning were held by the ARBiH?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not inhabited by?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just I was interested in control over villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you control our witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe I do it the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You tell me which villages -- which numbers, so to speak, were controlled by the ARBiH at the beginning of June. Just mention the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the main combat operations began on the 8th of June, 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: No. They began on the 4th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On the 4th of June; okay. And could you tell me an approximately date when they ceased?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of June, an order came on the cessation of hostilities and the operations quietened down, but they hadn't ceased completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I was asking you when the combat operations had completely ceased.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: It is hard to answer that question. On the 10th, they eased, but there were incidents. The order came on the 10th to cease hostilities, and that is the date that is considered to be a cessation of hostilities. But after that, there were just occasional incidents or provocations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But what you're saying is that the lines were basically not significantly moved?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: The problem of lines is a key issue here. Actually, we had villages that were surrounded, so you can't call them combat lines, in the traditional sense, and a blockade of communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, after the 10th of June, 1993, about which villages the ARBiH had established control? Just refer to the numbers here. And if control remained as before the 8th of June, can you also refer to the villages? I'm interested in all villages held by the ARBiH on the 10th of June.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: All the villages marked on the map, on the 10th of June, were under the control of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So this applies to number 1 until number, or number 14 as well? I'm just trying to clarify.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: 13 as well -- no, 14 as well, it was constantly under the control of the Army of BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So is it fair to conclude that as a result of the combat activities starting, as you said, around 4 or 5 June 1993, the ARBiH controlled all of a sudden the southern part of the Bila Valley, meaning all the villages from 1 until 14?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, but before that the Army of BiH had lost four villages captured by HVO forces on the 5th, 6th and 7th of June. On the 5th, 6th and 7th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And regained them?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, but they were burned down and destroyed, and the population removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But the fact remains that through the combat activities at the beginning of June, the lower part of the Bila Valley was still under the control of the ARBiH; right?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I would call it the upper part of the Bila Valley, the upper part of the Bila River.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But we are referring to the map here depicted in front of you; right?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So to sum up, the combat operation at the beginning of June was a success for the ARBiH, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: At first, we had very high losses, and later on we achieved success.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You gained territory?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. First we lost some territory, and later we gained some territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you established control even over villages which you could not control before, such as Guca Gora, for example?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you, because we were talking so often about it, mark Hrasce with a "15" on this map, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You encircled it. Could you mark a "15" next to the circle, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that in this corner of the map, meaning this elevation point marked with "15," elevation point Hrasce, there was one of the last remaining pockets of the HVO after the offensive at the beginning of -- the successful offensive at the beginning of June?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders this map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number. This is now D1044; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, D1044.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit number 1213.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We can maybe have the map still displayed for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You explained to us that you were blocked in Krpeljici, number 5 on this map, since 28 May 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if I understood your testimony yesterday correctly, the blockade of Krpeljici was lifted sometime in the night between the 8th and 9th of June, probably in the early-morning hours of the 9th of June; correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, but only one side of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So access was possible to Krpeljici from one side of it. Could you maybe indicate, by an arrow, from which side access was possible?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you maybe draw the arrow a little bit clearer, because I don't see exactly from which side.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. So is it fair to say that Krpeljici was deblocked from the location of Radonjici?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And Radonjici is marked by number 7 here on the map?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if I understood you correctly, until that lifting of the blockade in the early hours of 9th of June, you could not leave Krpeljici?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you could not participate, therefore, in any outside activities and in combat activities going on in some of the villages outside Krpeljici?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And from Krpeljici, you had no direct view of Maline?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. You can't see Maline.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There are, in fact, two mountains, elevation 851 and elevation 770, which blocked the view, is it?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So, in other words, on the 8th of June, while you were still in an encirclement, you could not see any combat activities going on in the area of Maline, could you?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You were talking about the forces lifting the blockade of Krpeljici from the direction of Radonjici. Could you confirm that the 1st Battalion -- or elements of the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade lifted the blockade of Krpeljici?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: No. The blockade of Krpeljici was lifted by the population, not as a formation, not as a battalion, but the people living in the villages that were attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you confirm that elements of the 4th Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade were also lifting -- or were lifting the blockade of Krpeljici?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Some elements, yes, but as the local people living there. The brigade at that time did not function as a military unit. These were the villages of Dub, Visnjevo, Suhi Dol, et cetera, et cetera. So the population just rose up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But can you confirm that elements of the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade were at least lifting or attacking -- sorry, I will rephrase. That elements of the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade were engaged in combat activities in the area of Bukovica, Bandol, Hrasce and Radojcici?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: No, I have to repeat, we were blocked in Krpeljici and the forces that came and lifted the blockade of Krpeljici were the local people living in the villages that I mentioned earlier, and no unit at that time functioned within the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I -- sorry, sir, Mr. Husic. Are you saying that people from Dub, and now there's a new name here which we haven't seen on the map, Visnjevo, Suhi Dol and other villages, came and lifted the blockade in Krpeljici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, do you remember seeing an investigator and myself last week in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do you remember that you -- or we were -- or you were giving us a statement last week?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We didn't get a translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And as the result of your meeting us in Sarajevo, as a result of your statement, we basically gave you -- I rephrase that, please. And we produced what you told us in form of a statement in the Bosnian language, which you could read and study, could you?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you were in a position to make any correction you wanted to make?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And we recorded, in your own language, every change you wished to make, did we?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you then were in a position to read again the statement before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we please have PT6254. Maybe before we do that, I was just informed that there was the arrow drawn on the map. Maybe we can save the arrow, if this is at all possible, before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't want to save the rest of the numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise. I had moved earlier to have the map admitted, and only afterwards the arrow was drawn. I didn't expect it at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. No, that's fine. So you want this map to be made -- given an exhibit number again with the arrow on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, maybe we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And could we give --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Suppress the earlier one, if it's possible. I don't know whether it's technically possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, this D1044, now with the arrow on it, is again admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit 1214.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we now please display PT6254.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this as the statement, in the Bosnian language, which you signed last week, Mr. Husic?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we please move to paragraph 8 now. That's page 3, probably, of the Bosnian version and page 3 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We can see, first of all, if you look at paragraph seven, you talk about the deblockade of Krpeljici, and then you go on in paragraph 8, and I will read it to you: "Only one part of the 1st and of the 4th Battalion of the 306th Brigade which were not engaged on the front line in Vlasic against the Chetniks, together with the civilians from the villages who were armed, moved to lift the blockade of the surrounded and attacked villages of Bukovica, Krpeljici, Bandol, Ricice, Radonjici, Maline and Mosor." Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I remember, and that is what I'm still claiming. So we did not operate as a unit, but as the people -- local people from that area who were also members of these battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But now you're saying "who were also members of these battalions." A moment ago, I asked you whether elements of the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade were involved in lifting the blockade of Krpeljici, and you didn't confirm it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. I apologise to the witness. The Prosecutor did not ask whether there were members of, but whether they were part of the battalion, the 306th, and parts of the 4th Battalion, which is not the same thing, if you ask whether elements of that battalion or members. Those are two different things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm just trying to locate the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe I can be of help. That's on page 25, lines 1 through 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But I'm interested in my question on 25, line 10, and I said: "Sorry, I will rephrase --" Sorry, 25, line 8: "Can you confirm that elements of the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade were at least lifting or attacking -- sorry, I will rephrase. That elements of the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade were engaged in combat activities in the area of Bukovica, Bandol, Hrasce," and then it's illegible, and before -- on page 24, line 19, I asked: "Could you confirm that the 1st Battalion or elements of the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade lifted the blockade of Krpeljici?" I was expressly asking for elements of the 1st Battalion, and you said: "No, the blockade of Krpeljici was lifted by the population, not as a formation, not as a battalion, but the people in the villages that were attacked." Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. We still have an objection on the table. Madam Vidovic was on her feet, but I wanted you to finish what you were saying before I asked her. Madam Vidovic, you were -- I thought you were on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, because it seems to me that the witness is getting confused on this matter. From what Mr. Neuner just read, it's completely clear that he had asked about elements of the battalion as formations, in other words, and not about individual members of those battalions. Those are not the same thing. In fact, the witness already gave his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, what I'm hearing the witness saying is that, yes, individuals belonging to the 1st and maybe the 4th Battalion of the 306th Brigade did assist in the liberation of Krpeljici, but they did so in their individual capacity. They came probably with their weapons and maybe also their uniforms, but they were not under command. So maybe we can confirm with the witness if this is correctly understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But that is precisely Madam Vidovic's basis for objection. You see, when you say "elements," you're talking of part of a unit; in other words, you are saying somebody who is in control of the unit said, "This part of the unit, go and liberate the place." But he's saying, "No, no, no, no such part of a unit came. Individual members who were members of the village, who were villagers, but some of whom did belong to the battalions."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I fully agree with this, but I'm only following up on what the witness has told me a week ago, where he expressly said one part of the 1st and 4th Battalion. That's why I was careful in putting it to him, were there elements, because he said a part of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I didn't want to lead him on this point, so to speak, but rather get an answer, and what I got was a flat denial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is true. We're just explaining the answer as it is on the record. You can confront him with his statement, if you so wish. Madam Vidovic -- yes, ma'am, can we hear you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my objection still stands. The Prosecutor is confusing the witness. In the next -- here he was insisting on paragraph 8, but in the next paragraph, paragraph 9, you have the explanation of what the witness said here in the courtroom, and he says that these were informal groups. In the next paragraph already, the witness is expanding on his position, so he should not be confused here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Madam Vidovic. I guess Mr. Neuner is asking the witness about paragraph 8. If you want to draw the attention of the witness to paragraph 9, you can do so in re-examination. It cannot be the basis of an objection. You may proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm just taking issue at this moment with your answer when I was asking for elements of the 1st Battalion. When you answered on page 24, line 23: "No, the blockade of Krpeljici was lifted by the population, not as a formation, not as a battalion, but the people living in the villages that were attacked," but could you confirm that last week you said a slightly different variant, that parts of the 1st and the 4th Battalion of the 306th Brigade, together with some civilians, were indeed lifting the blockade of Krpeljici?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is stated here in the eighth paragraph, I did say, but there is no mention of what you asked about the 1st and 4th battalions. In this statement, what I spoke about was just a small number of individuals who were from the complement of the 1st and 4th Battalions, who were in their villages, and who were able to participate in this lifting of the blockade. If your question was in there, you could have seen that from it, the same way as you are insinuating and insisting all the time that the conflict started on the 8th, and I kept repeating that the blockade and the attack really began on the 28th of May already, and on the 4th of June the villages were attacked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but, Witness, the statement -- in the witness statement you gave before today's testimony, you did not mention elements from the 2nd Battalion who were locals. You instead spoke about elements that were not involved on the front line in Vlasic against the Chetniks. So as far as I can see, there is certainly a major discrepancy between these two statements you made.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not see the difference. I don't understand what the difference is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would this be a convenient time? Maybe when we come back, we can begin to see things better. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, I want to stay for a moment with you in Krpeljici, in this time period when you were blocked, but I want to move away from the question who deblocked to -- who deblocked Krpeljici to the next issue, and that is whether communications were possible in the time period when you were blocked from the 28th of May, 1993, until the early morning of the 9th of June, 1993. And yesterday, I just want to remind you, you testified, and this was at the end of page 18 -- you got the question: "Did you or did you not have contacts with a part of the Command of the 306th Brigade in Rudnik?" And then on page 19, you responded to that question: "Only until the end of May. As of June 1st, we did not have contacts with any of our units." And you were later on, on the same page, asked to clarify that, and you said: "I did say the 2nd of June, because on the 2nd of June attacks began on these villages, and that was when all the communication was cut off." You were then asked again about communications. I ask you now about the situation in the corps. Did you have contacts with the corps, you from the place where you were blocked off. And you responded on page 19, line 24: "No, not with the corps or with anyone else." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And then you were shown a serious of documents, Exhibit 999, Exhibit 258 and Exhibit 1001, and you were asked, so to speak, about your knowledge about these documents. And on that occasion, I think it was Exhibit 999, you said -- this is page 20, line 19 until 22: "As of the 28th, I was continuously with the commander ..." I skip a part of the sentence, and then it says: " ... we didn't have contacts with anyone." Do you remember having said this?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. As of May 1st, with no one -- June 1st, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And today you're also sticking to this version of the events?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Husic, having testified on the 28th of October, 2004, here at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the proceedings relating to Hadzihasanovic and Kubura?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that at that time, you had a reasonably good recollection of the events?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It may be that your memory was fresher in 2004 than it is today?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to put something to you, and this is PT2653. It's a transcript portion which is in English, unfortunately, only, but I will read it to you so that it gets translated. And I need page 118, please. For the record, it is transcript page 10896. And while it comes up, just to give an introduction, I will read a part of line 8 so that we can get the context. It's -- thank you. On line 8, we see you talk about, in your answer: "The blockade of the part of the command in Krpeljici ..." And you were asked, on line 21, if you could scroll down on that page, please, the following question: "Can you tell us, please, what is your personal knowledge of what was happening on the 8th of June?" And your answer is: "On the 8th of June, at one moment the whole Bila Valley, one can say, was aflame. The shooting that one could hear from all the other place and from time to time became more intense." And if you could flip the page: "And on that particular day, it was very intense. We didn't know what was going on. And like the previous day, we cried for help. We sent requests for help to the 3rd Corps, but we did not receive any reply. And as a matter of fact, the only thing we could do was to instruct every village to defend themselves with what little strength they have. After that, we received information that our forces, which we kept in the reserve," and so on. And two lines further down, it says: " ... warned us that there might have been an attack from Mount Vlasic ..." Do you remember testifying this at the time?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree that according to this version of the event, you had contacts from Krpeljici with the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. I don't see how one can conclude from this text that they were in contact with the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Well, it just says here, on page 10897, lines 2 and 3: "We sent requests for help to the 3rd Corps, but we did not receive any reply."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We saw a dispatch yesterday that was sent from a part of the Command of the 306th Mountain Brigade which was at the Rudnik feature. They were the only ones who had contact with the 3rd Corps, and based on what they had seen and heard, as we had in Krpeljici, they called for help.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. So your testimony is that from Rudnik, they could contact the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if I go down one line more, "the only thing we could to," you testified, and that's lines 3 and 4, "was to instruct every village to defend themselves with what little strength they have. After that, we received information that our forces," so on and so forth, "warned us again." Doesn't that suggest that you, in fact, had communication from Krpeljici?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: No. On the 28th, we were blocked off in Krpeljici, and until the beginning of the conflict that started on the 1st and 2nd, and intensified on the 4th, we, with one part, with the villages in the immediate surrounding area, we had contact with them, and this contact functioned until the 1st of May. So between the 28th of May and the 1st of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Can we just go back to the previous page. Go down to the bottom of the page. Mr. Husic, you are talking about first the 28th of May and the 1st of June. This question that is on this transcript, to which you were answering, refers to the 8th of June. Could you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 8th of June, there was general fighting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wait a minute. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a portion of the transcript from the Hadzihasanovic case. The witness cannot speak English, so how could he see?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, this, I think, Mr. Neuner said he was going to read. But, anyway, then let me make you aware, Mr. Husic, that the answer that was being read to you was to a question which says: "Can you tell us, please, what is your personal knowledge of what was happening on the 8th of June?" And your answer started by saying: "On the 8th of June ..." Do you agree with that? That's what you said in the Hadzihasanovic case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We're not talking about the 28th of May or the 1st of June, which is what you are now telling us about. Can you answer the question about the 8th of June, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 8th of June, we did not have any contact with anyone. The fighting was ongoing throughout the Bila Valley.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, the question that was being put to you was, if you can turn to the next page again, can it be inferred that you did have communication with the outside world, I'm putting those words in, because you have been told that you said on that day: "We sent requests for help to the 3rd Corps, but we did not receive any reply, and as a matter of fact the only thing we could do was to instruct every village to defend themselves with what little strength they have." Now, this is what you testified about relating to the 8th of June, sir, not the 28th of May, not the 1st of June. That's the question that's being put to you. Can it be inferred that you did have communication?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, absolutely not. We didn't have any communication. I was talking about the broader context that preceded the 8th of June, and that is an imprecision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're not being asked about the broader context preceding the 8th of June, you're being asked about the 8th of June. Now, please listen to the question and answer the question. Don't formulate your own question and answer your own question. Mr. Neuner, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. You told us that you cried for help to the corps and that you did not receive any reply. Do you know whether the 3rd Corps actually received your request for help?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I can't know that, whether they received our request for aid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, regarding communications on that day, on the 8th of June, you've mentioned difficulties, the blockade. This could have prevented the 3rd Corps from receiving your requests for help, or did you have a way to make sure that they were going to receive your request, even if there were some difficulties in communicating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said we sent a request, I was referring to the 306th Mountain Brigade, part of whose command was surrounded at Rudnik. The commander and those of us who were surrounded, his chief of staff and two assistants, at the time had no contact even with that part of the 306th or the corps. So I don't know anything that was happening outside of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm not sure of the significance of the witness being able to send messages to the Corps Command, but I'll get back to that. Before I ask this question to the Prosecution, I would like to just clarify with the witness. The call you sent for help to the 3rd Corps, was that a call made by radio or how was it dispatched? How did you seek to communicate with the 3rd Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This part of the command, the command of the chief of staff, myself and another assistant, we didn't do that. It was the officers on duty in the Command of the 306th Mountain Brigade at Rudnik. Yesterday, we were able to see one such document as a telegram sent to the corps. We saw this during the proceedings. I don't know the exact date, but it was before the 8th of June, maybe the 1st or 2nd or 3rd of June. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right, because I just need to be sure about the means you had at your disposal for communicating with the outside world when you were sitting there in Krpeljici. You could send scouts out, or you can do it by radio, you can do it by telegram, you can do it by any number of ways, so I'm asking what -- how did you actually try to call for help, or how did the Brigade Command seek assistance? You told us that there was a telegram sent. That is one way. Were you also able to reach the 3rd Corps by radio, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not from Krpeljici. I'm not an expert on communications, but I will do my best to explain this question. While we were blocked in Krpeljici, we had a system of courier, message links, telephone links, with a inductor military telephone, and radio communications, using the means of communication of the Yugoslav People's Army, and I can't really tell you what kind of device that was. And then on the first or second day of the blockade, the 29th and the 30th of May, we did occasionally have communication. The messenger could no longer leave, but the telephone lines were still working, not with the Command at Rudnik, but that was the base of the battalion and battalions had such links. So we contacted the Battalion Command, and they communicated with Rudnik. However, on the 2nd of May, when the all-out attack started -- June, I'm sorry -- all telephone lines were down. After that, occasionally we had radio communication not with the Command at Rudnik, because the Command at Rudnik did not have that link, but we had three villages on the outskirts, Velika Bukovica, Bandol and Radonjici. They had JNA radio devices, and there was one radio device in Krpeljici. But when the conflict started, HVO forces at Velika Bukovica had a large radio device, I don't know what type it is, on a truck, and it could completely block and prevent communication with the small radio devices that we had. So I claim with full responsibility from the 2nd of May -- no, the 2nd of June, we did not have any communications. When I said that we communicated with the corps, I meant that our duty officers at Rudnik, three of them, who are actually civilians but in those days were officers, they had some sort of contact with the 3rd Corps, and we saw yesterday the telegrams they sent from the Command at Rudnik. However, we, the commander, the chief of staff, myself and another colleague, and the entire battalion, could not communicate with them, or the corps, or with anyone else, except for the village of Krpeljici itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This was very illustrative. Now remind us, Mr. Neuner, what is the importance of all of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The importance, in the Prosecution's position, is that the brigade commander was there on that day, and combat operations were going on from Mehurici via Maline and other villages, ultimately lifting the blockade of Krpeljici, and certainly in the aftermath of these combat operations, prisoners of war had been taken as a result of these combat operations, and it is important to show command and control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Well, I understand where you are going, but I'm not sure I'm able to conclude that command and control was intact, from having this witness testifying that for seven or 8 days they were cut off in Krpeljici. That was just my point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you will understand that it is very important for the Defence to know what the position of the Prosecution is. From what the Prosecution here said, and that is that their position is that the brigade commander was there, we want to know what he means "there," when he says "there," does he mean in Krpeljici or in Maline, so we know how to respond as the Defence in this connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I understood this witness's testimony correctly, the brigade commander was in Krpeljici on the 8th of June, until he was deblocked. And we had also other witnesses testifying about that situation and testifying about communications with the brigade commander in this time period.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, if I can go on, is it fair to say that the communication, which were partially blocked by that truck from the HVO, they went on and off, meaning sometimes it was blocked, sometimes not, depending on whether the truck worked or not?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: From the 28th of May until the 2nd of June, it did work occasionally. As of the 2nd of May again, when the fighting intensified, the communications no longer worked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I intervene. At the number of places, we keep talking of the 2nd of May, and then we correct "2nd of June." Now, this time we're saying again "2nd of May," and there's no correction. Is it the 2nd of May we're referring to or is it the 2nd of June? Are you referring to the 2nd of June, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I sincerely do. It's the 2nd of June I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I just want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But I also want you to bear in mind that the questions from the lawyer relate to the 8th of June. So if you keep taking us back to the 2nd of June, you are really not answering the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I could just for a moment have the statement which was taken last week being displayed. That's PT6524. And I'm interested in paragraph 4, where you talk about: "We, as part of the 306th Brigade, were completely cut off from the rest of the command of the brigade ..." And then in the second sentence, you say: "During one time period, we could use military induction telephones, but they were also cut off following the begins of clashes. From then on, we were using former JNA radio devices. With Mehurici, we could only communicate through radio device. Actually, the HVO had a communication centre in the area of Bukovica which was interfering with our communication, so it went on and off." So is it correct it went also on, the radio communication; you could use it from time to time?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: We were speaking of the period of time from the 28th of May until the 8th of June, and I described what happened during that time period, and I said clearly and explicitly that from the moment the conflict became massive, that was the 2nd of May, we no longer had any communication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're referring to the 2nd of May again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2nd of June, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I can just put the sentences again to you, you're talking, in the second sentence, about: "During one time period, we could use military induction telephones, but they were also cut off following the begins of the clashes." And that's the 2nd of June you're always referring to, right, the beginning of the clashes; correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And then you go on to say: "From then on, we were using these former JNA radio devices." And in the next sentence, you're clearly referring here to the time period after the clashes started. The HVO was interfering, but it went on and off the communication; so it was working, but not the whole time; correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: It worked from the beginning of the blockade until the beginning of the clashes. I'm repeating myself for the 10th time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then you're changing, in the Prosecution's view, the meaning of that last sentence, but I will move on to my last topic, which is the investigation or the course of the investigation into the incident which had happened when the group of Croats was escorted towards Mehurici and some Croats were taken away on the way. And with regard to the course of the investigation, I want to recall what you said yesterday on page 39, lines 4 until 8, "and at this time, because of the all the disinformation we mentioned, mention was made of a huge number of people, tens of people killed in different areas, so at this time we could not find out anything more in any detail." And then you were asked: "Was it established, according to what you know, who were the perpetrators -- who the perpetrators were or not?" And your answer is: "No. We really wanted to establish this, and both the police and the Security Service, but also other services of the brigade, because this was addressed to us, this was at our expense because it happened in our area of responsibility. All of these services really wanted to establish the truth. I know this because we sent policemen who had been intercepted. We sent them to try and identify among these -- from among these armed groups to identify the people by observing those areas where they moved and through which they were moved. However, we were never able to find out the exact information." You remember having said this?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you have, in detail, described the different steps undertaken and the different services being involved in the investigation, have you?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: That there was the Military Security Service involved, that policemen were sent, that they were intercepted, that they tried to identify them, the persons, so step by step you're listing the different measures involved or employed; correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I just refer now to what you said in the Hadzihasanovic and Kubura case, and this is -- if we can have PT6253, please, on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, before we get PT6253 on the screen, I see we are now at PT6254 a second time. Do you want it admitted or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I believe I read the relevant portions into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you don't need it admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And therefore it is already captured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we have from PT6253 now, transcript pages 10934. Later on, we will swap the page to 10935.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you were getting here a question from Judge Swart, and the investigation relates to two investigations at the same time, the investigation into the Miletici events as well as the investigation into the Maline events. I can explain that at the time Miletici and Maline were the subject of the Hadzihasanovic trial, so for the purposes of this hearing today, I'm only interested in the part of your answer which relates to Maline and the course of the investigation there. And if we could go to line 12 -- or line 14, Judge Swart is asking you first, in one question, as I said about two investigations at the same time: "The report on the events in Miletici which you were not involved in an investigation, is this also true for the report that has been made in the investigation that has been carried out for Maline? Were you also not involved in that investigation?" And the relevant part of the answer is: At the beginning, you are referring to Miletici. If I can just go directly to the part related to Maline, that's on line 22 of your answer: "And when it comes to Maline," you said, "there was combat going on. The combat went on for 20 days at the time. And the first information I received about Maline, as I've already said, arrived on the 12th of June." And then you go on to say, and we need to swap the page, please, and this is line 2: "Only later on the investigation carried out by the Military Security Service did define everything and provided more details. However, I did not follow the course of this investigation because I was prevented from doing that by the combat activities." Do you remember having testified this?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So if you had said in the Hadzihasanovic trial you were prevented from combat activities from following the course of the investigation, how could you say that certain steps had been undertaken by the Military Security Service, and you were listing these steps?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC
utterances.text: The body for morale never takes part in any investigation, because that is the job of the security services. But due to the sensitivity of the issue, the assistant commander for security informed all members of the Command in detail, and that's what I'm talking about. We all knew what the investigation was about, how far it had progressed. We wanted it to be successful so that any suspicions regarding the brigade should be eliminated, to show that our members had not committed those acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Why didn't you say so in the Hadzihasanovic trial, when you were asked by the Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic. Sorry, sir. Your lawyer is on her feet. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The Prosecutor is confusing the witness. In the Hadzihasanovic case, the witness said: "I did not follow the course of the investigation," and he hasn't said anything different during his testimony here. So I would appeal to the Prosecutor not to confuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But if the witness is talking about the different steps which have been undertaken by the Military Security Service, how can he do that if he hasn't followed the investigation? That's my question I tried to elicit. That's all I want to establish.
